rationale: This Stanford Bubblesort sample is a tiny, loop-intensive integer program with no profiled call graph or globals, so the weight table favors cheap, arithmetic-oriented passes and downweights ones whose benefit depends on rich call/global structure. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain because bubble sort is dominated by comparisons, swaps, and index arithmetic that substitution obfuscates effectively at low risk; its low RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights reflect that the costs are minor and the tiny binary has a large size budget. FLA is kept strong (flattening the nested loop nest is the biggest reverse-engineering deterrent here) with a moderately elevated RuntimeCost weight since the sort loop is hot, and SPLIT is enabled cheaply to fragment basic blocks and amplify FLA/SUB. BCF is included at moderate weight — opaque predicates add meaningful confusion but its runtime overhead on the inner loop justifies a raised RuntimeCost weight. IBR is retained at low-moderate weight only to diversify loop back-edges, with an elevated CorrectnessRisk weight since indirect branches on tight loop back-edges are the likeliest correctness hazard. ICALL and IGV are omitted entirely: with essentially no indirect-call candidates or global variable traffic in a single-file sort, they add overhead and risk without proportionate security or diversity gain.
